failure_summary.description: The hotel search result was not assigned to a variable or saved to cache.
The explicit solo-traveler detail was not mapped to the hotel's supported traveler-count field.

patch.reasoning: Result binding and caching are already explicitly required, so repeating that instruction is unlikely to address this failure. Clarifying the mapping from “solo” to a supported traveler-count field makes the omitted hotel parameter more actionable without inferring a room count.

edits.target: - Carry forward relevant details from the conversation and include explicitly supplied criteria in the appropriate call. Send only schema-supported parameters; do not infer amenities, ratings, or other preferences. Do not infer exact party or room counts from broad descriptions such as “family.” Treat “solo” as one traveler only when a supported traveler-count field is available; do not infer a room count from it. A traveler count is not a flight-search parameter unless the schema provides one.
edits.content: - Carry forward relevant details from the conversation and include explicitly supplied criteria in the appropriate call. Send only schema-supported parameters; do not infer amenities, ratings, or other preferences. Do not infer exact party or room counts from broad descriptions such as “family.” When the user says “solo,” set a supported traveler-count field to 1 (for example, `num_people=1` in a hotel search); do not infer a room count from it. A traveler count is not a flight-search parameter unless the schema provides one.
